_comment: M00 / T4 - Runtime world configuration. Read by src/runtime/world/world_config.gd.

M01: config_version 2 adds worldgen_version + modules override block; quality_tier now owns concrete budgets (see WorldConfig.TIER_BUDGETS) and view_distance_chunks is an OVERRIDE of the tier default (8 here, tier 'low' default 6) - the HUD shows which won.
In M00 only `seed`, `view_distance_chunks` and `generator` actually change what you
see on screen; the rest are read, validated and recorded so that later milestones
(M01 spine, M02 planetary heightfields) inherit a stable contract instead of
inventing one. See docs/ARCHITECTURE.md for why the 384-block height matters.
seed                  Integer seed for EVERY generator. No global randf anywhere.
generator             'native_cb' (DEFAULT: the engine's own multipass callback running
the resolved module pipeline), 'experimental_columns' (self-hosted
columns, same pipeline, no engine pass limits, ~30x slower), or the
frozen M00 baselines 'graph' / 'noise2d' which execute their own
fixed maths and IGNORE the modules. Cycled with F3, which skips the
two baselines unless allow_legacy_baseline is true.
allow_legacy_baseline false (default). Booting on 'graph' or 'noise2d' requires true, and
the world then prints that the enabled modules will not run. This is
the fail-closed gate for M01's evidence E2: a backend that ignores
the modules cannot be a module pipeline's default.
allow_broken_pipeline false (default). A pipeline that does not resolve refuses to boot.
There is deliberately NO fallback generator: M01 quietly rebuilt on
noise2d, turning 'the pipeline is broken' into 'the world is flat
but boots', which is the failure mode this project exists to prevent.
view_distance_chunks  Horizontal view distance in 16-block data blocks. Cycled F4.
quality_tier          'low' | 'medium' | 'high'. Validated and shown on the HUD.
In M00 it deliberately does NOT override view_distance_chunks:
one knob, one owner. Mapping tiers to concrete chunk/memory
budgets is M10 (distant terrain) / M14 (art lock) work.
world_y_max is EXCLUSIVE: 320 means the highest buildable block index is 319 and the
world is exactly 384 blocks tall (320 - (-64)).

streaming._comment2: type_depth_bits=8 halves the TYPE channel versus the engine default of 16-bit (verified with tools/probe_generators.gd P6). Ceiling is 255 block ids; revisit when attribute variants need more (M09+).
streaming._comment: view_distance_vertical_ratio is VoxelViewer's own knob (verified in docs/reports/voxel_api_dump.json). It is the single most important lever for a 384-block-tall world on a phone: 1.0 loads the full column, 0.5 halves the vertical chunk count.
streaming._vertical_ratio_note: Measured with tools/probe_vratio.gd: on VoxelTerrain (not just VoxelLodTerrain as the 1.7 docs claim) this ratio scales the VIEWER's vertical streaming volume. At 1.0 a player who flies ~200 m up loses the terrain entirely (0 blocks loaded at y=264, vd=8). 2.0 keeps the surface column streamed while flying and costs nothing on the ground (410 blocks either way, because vertical selection follows the surface).

gen_params._comment: M00 terrain shape, read ONLY by the two legacy baselines (graph, noise2d). The modular backends take their numbers from the module .tres files in content/modules/ instead; while the graph stays the golden reference these two must agree, and the determinism suite fails loudly if they drift (native_cb vs graph over 64 + 256 origins). Deliberately simple rolling hills - biomes/climate/erosion are M02+.
